parsed.explanation: No criminal provision reaches trans identity or expression; no documented enforcement, police targeting, facility rule, or border friction against trans visitors. The state has no prison system, so custody-placement risk is structurally minimal. Against this, the record is thin and the governing institution's posture is doctrinally hostile: 'gender theory' framed as dangerous, rejection of gay diplomats, diplomatic lobbying against LGBT protections, no legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination coverage. These are climate signals and resident-facing gaps, not traveler exposures — but in a thin-data jurisdiction the doctrinal hostility plus total absence of protective machinery and of any documented recourse means silence is not proof of safety. Extrapolating: no enforcement lever exists, but a visitor outed faces no protection and an institutionally disapproving climate. This sits above dead-letter-statute-plus-acceptance profiles (0.65-C lacks the active doctrinal hostility) but well below jurisdictions with documented exposures. A modest 0.65–0.70 placement: no known traveler-facing harm, but unresolved facility/screening questions and an unfriendly governing tone.
